fields.meta_description: Build a boo basket questionnaire for coworkers, teachers, or neighbors that tracks who is booed and keeps every answer in a database you own.
fields.h1: Build a Boo Basket Questionnaire That Tells Booers What to Buy
fields.hero_description: Build a boo basket questionnaire that sends each person's candy picks and allergies to whoever is building their basket.
fields.features_heading: What the Basket Builder Needs to Know
fields.features_subheading: A boo basket questionnaire turns a guess about someone's taste into a list of things they like. Emergent builds the app around it.
fields.feature_1:
Questions drafted from one sentence

Describe the group and the budget, such as 16 coworkers with a $20 limit. Emergent builds the questions and the database behind them, then changes both when you ask in plain English.
fields.feature_2:
Answers given one screen at a time

A teacher can finish it between classes when each question gets its own screen. Candy picks take one tap, and a longer box holds the stores and hobbies she wants mentioned.
fields.feature_3:
Allergies shown before anyone shops

Ask about allergies and foods to skip near the top of the questionnaire. The app puts that answer first on the page the basket builder reads, above the candy and the favorite stores.
fields.feature_4:
Email reminders before delivery day

Send each boo buddy an email reminder 3 days before delivery day. The organizer gets an in-app alert each time a basket is marked delivered and can see who has not delivered yet.
fields.feature_5:
Every answer kept, with no response cap

Answers land in a database you own, one row per person, and there is no cap on responses. Reopen the questionnaire next October and last year's answers are still there to compare.
fields.feature_6:
Code you can take to your own repo

On paid plans, export the full code to your GitHub repository. A gift shop that sells boo baskets can host its order questionnaire next to its own website and keep building on it.

fields.usecase_heading: Where Boo Basket Answers End Up
fields.tab_content_1:
Reveal week starts with three buddies who owe a basket

Kestrel Bay Title pairs its 16 employees as boo buddies in early October, after everyone answers the questionnaire. Office manager Bettina Rowe tracks the swap on one dashboard. With 2 days left before the October 30 reveal, 13 baskets are marked delivered and 3 are still due, each listed with the buddy who owes it.
fields.tab_content_2:
Ms. Fosse is claimed by Priya, who gets her answers

Room parents at Thornbury Middle School each boo one of the 24 teachers who filled in the questionnaire. Priya Kessler picks Ms. Fosse, and the form marks her taken so no other parent can choose her. Priya then sees what Ms. Fosse wrote: she loves sour gummies and avoids dairy.
fields.tab_content_3:
The next family only sees houses that said yes

Larchmere Court runs a booing chain each October, and the questionnaire asks every household whether it wants to be booed. Of 42 households, 35 said yes. A family that gets booed opens the list of houses still waiting, and the 7 that opted out never appear on it. House No. 11 is marked with a peanut allergy.
fields.tab_content_4:
Each order lands with what the recipient likes

Maren Tolle sells boo baskets at Wickbury Gift Co. in a $45 size and a $75 size. Buyers answer for the person getting the basket. Wren Delacroix ordered a $75 basket for her sister. Maren's email shows the sister's favorite candy, peanut butter cups, and one scent to leave out: pumpkin spice. Pickup is October 28.

fields.howto_title: How to Make a Boo Basket Questionnaire
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to make a boo basket questionnaire that gives every basket builder a short, usable list, then build it with Emergent.
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Ask about things a person can buy
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 State the budget and the date
fields.howto_step_1_des: Decide who reads the answers before you write a single question. In an office swap, each buddy reads one coworker's answers. When a shop takes orders, the buyer answers on behalf of someone else, and the questions have to work for that.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Keep every question tied to something that fits in a basket: a favorite candy, a salty snack, a drink order, a candle scent, a color. Skip questions like a favorite memory, because nobody can shop from the answer.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Ask about allergies and foods the person avoids in the first two questions, while attention is fresh. Make the field required, with a clear none option, and show it at the top of what the basket builder reads.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Print the spending limit and the delivery deadline on the first screen, such as $20 per basket by October 30. Respondents answer differently when they know the basket is small, and builders stop guessing how much to spend.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Add a plain yes or no question about whether the person wants a basket at all. A coworker on a diet or a household that skips Halloween can opt out, and nobody has to explain it to the organizer.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Send it in the first week of October
fields.howto_step_6_des: Give respondents a week to answer and builders 2 weeks to shop. Sending the link in the first days of October leaves room for a reminder to anyone who has not answered, plus time for deliveries before Halloween.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Test it with two people first
fields.howto_step_7_des: Describe the questionnaire to Emergent, then have two friends fill it in on their phones. Read their answers as if you were shopping for them. Change any question that left you unsure what to buy before the real link goes out.

faq_plan.q: What is a boo basket questionnaire?
faq_plan.a: A boo basket questionnaire is a short set of questions about what someone likes, answered before a boo basket is put together for them. A boo basket is a container filled with Halloween-themed treats and small gifts, and the answers tell the builder which treats and gifts to choose.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a boo basket questionnaire?
faq_plan.a: Describe it to Emergent's AI form builder in a sentence or two: who answers, who builds the baskets, the budget, and the delivery date. Emergent builds the questionnaire and its database, plus any pairing or claiming logic, and you change any of it by asking in plain English.

faq_plan.q: What questions should a boo basket questionnaire ask?
faq_plan.a: Ask for two candies they love and one they will not eat, a coffee order, and a scent for a candle. Add sock or pajama size if clothing might go in the basket, plus one open box for a hobby. Cap it at about ten questions.

faq_plan.q: Should a business send a boo basket questionnaire to its clients?
faq_plan.a: Yes, if the business plans to send client boo baskets, since the answers stop it from guessing. Keep it to five questions about the person, not the company. A brand questionnaire is a different tool: it asks a client about their business and audience before design work starts.

faq_plan.q: How do I keep boo buddy pairs secret on a boo basket questionnaire?
faq_plan.a: Keep the pair list visible only to the organizer, and show each person their own buddy's answers and nothing else. Email each buddy separately instead of posting the pairs in a shared channel. In an app Emergent builds, the pairs and the answers sit in a database you own.

faq_plan.q: How long should a boo basket questionnaire stay open?
faq_plan.a: Keep it open for about a week. Close it at least 2 weeks before the delivery date, and send one reminder 3 days before it closes to anyone still missing. Late answers after the pairs go out leave a buddy shopping blind.

faq_plan.q: Can I reuse a boo basket questionnaire for other gifts?
faq_plan.a: Yes, once you drop the spending limit and the deadline. What is left is a favorite things questionnaire, which can stay on file all year for birthdays and thank-you gifts. Ask people to update their answers each fall, since tastes and allergies change.

faq_plan.q: How do I use a boo basket questionnaire for a neighborhood booing chain?
faq_plan.a: Ask every household one question first: do you want to be booed? In the classic game, a basket is left in secret on a doorstep, and the recipient then creates a basket for someone else, allowing the Halloween surprise to spread from house to house. A list of houses that said yes keeps the chain off doors that opted out.

faq_plan.q: Should a boo basket questionnaire for adults ask different questions?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Adults are easier to shop for when you ask about coffee or tea, wine or no alcohol, a self-care item they like, and a sock or sweatshirt size. Drop the toy and coloring book questions that suit a basket for kids.

faq_plan.q: Can a boo basket questionnaire live on my gift shop's website?
faq_plan.a: Yes. The questionnaire Emergent builds can run on your own domain, and custom domains are included and use credits. If the shop is also planning a redesign, send your designer a website design questionnaire separately, because it asks about pages and branding, not candy.

plan.angle: The top 10 for boo basket questionnaire is printables and Etsy sheets: a list of blanks someone fills in and hands to whoever builds the basket. None of them handles what organizers actually juggle in October: pairing buddies, knowing who has been booed, skipping houses that opted out, or taking custom basket orders. This page shows the questionnaire as a small app for four real boo basket jobs, an office buddy swap, a school's teachers, a street's booing chain and a gift shop's orders, and the FAQ covers what to ask, who sees the answers and when to send it.
